For a **plug-in backup that can run normal enclosure heating**, the search results recommend the **[BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)**. Its 2,073.6 Wh capacity is estimated to run a 100 W ceramic heat emitter for about a day when a thermostat cycles it on and off; a low-wattage heat mat could last longer. The listed price is $899, with a $44.95 code discount through the link. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage))

Before buying, check your heater’s wattage and the station’s AC output, then size for the outage you need to cover—runtime depends on how often the thermostat calls for heat. **Insulate the enclosure** to reduce heat loss, and keep an emergency heat plan ready; Petco also suggests wrapped warm-water bottles or chemical hand warmers as short-term options. ([Petco](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-pet-reptiles-during-a-power-outage))
